reconstructions.reconstructed_text: There are four aspects among mankind that perceive, as they perceive [all things that are hidden and revealed; and] without these four that are hidden in them [no man is able to perceive, for] they belong [to the whole of the living soul]. So, [by these four aspects a man perceives all things].
[The warmth] that is in the [heart] belongs to the fire. The darkness belongs to the abyss; but the light that perceives what is hidden in all these things, being clear, is the living air.

How shall the pupil of the eye perceive? While it perceives by day, yet come the night it shall not perceive. What mystery does this matter signify? The pupil of the eye shall not [perceive in the darkness; for] the mystery of the [eye] is the door [from] below [to the heights and to] the other four cardinal points. For in the [heights is that which is] above. He has [called forth his] great [evocations, and] they came down [from the heights into the] living [soul]. The First Man came forth from it and knew all things.
